scope: Previously retrieved public main accepted metadata; no authenticated board access or exhaustive absence claim

metadata.title: Read the status lamp's blink code, then swap the module it names
metadata.context: Servers and robots report which module failed as a blink pattern on a status LED; a service robot must read the pattern over time, replace the named field-replaceable unit and verify, without touching the healthy ones.
metadata.instruction: While you hold the white DIAG button the status lamp blinks the number of the failed socket (count the dots beside each socket); replace that module with the teal spare, then hold DIAG again until the lamp stays green.
metadata.setup: A rigid free-standing fixture (one 8.0 kg body, friction 1.0, not bolted down) on the station table (z = 74.8 cm) holds a 4-socket bus strip and a DIAG controller box. Four keyed sockets (pitch 7.0 cm, mouths at x = 24.0 cm, z = 2.5 cm above table) sit at y = -5.0 cm (socket 1, 1 dot), y = -12.0 cm (socket 2, 2 dots), y = -19.0 cm (socket 3, 3 dots), and y = -26.0 cm (socket 4, 4 dots), each with aluminium flange 56 x 42 x 6 mm, dark shell 38 x 30 x 24 mm, 30 x 18 mm cavity (1.0 mm clearance per side to 28 x 16 mm nose), 8 x 3 mm key slot, and 12 N/mm spring plunger (round 4 mm tip, 1.5 mm proud on +y wall). Controller box (140 x 120 x 40 mm, centre at x = 25.0 cm, y = 20.0 cm) holds a white DIAG button cap (36 x 36 x 12 mm, 4 g, centre at x = 22.0 cm, y = 20.0 cm, cap top 6.0 cm above the table at rest, 8 mm travel to a hard stop, soft 100 N/m spring) and a 60 mm diameter, 15 mm tall status lamp dome (centre at x = 28.5 cm, y = 20.0 cm; off = dark grey, blink = amber/yellow, verified = green, healthy missing = red). Four servo modules (80 g each, friction 0.8; 45 x 18 x 28 mm housing with grey band, steel nose 28 x 16 x 18 mm with key rib and detent groove) start seated in sockets 1 to 4 with nose pointing +x. One spare servo module with a teal band starts staged on the table at x = 38.0 cm, y = -15.0 cm.
metadata.scoring: Partial credit ladder: 0.25 if DIAG button is held >= 3 s once (held >= 60 control steps) or any module is touched / displaced > 5 mm or DIAG button depressed >= 2.0 mm; 0.50 if failed module (module 3) is out of socket 3 (depth < 16 mm, lateral offset > 1.5 mm, or angle error > 10.0 deg) with every healthy module (1, 2, 4) still seated; 0.75 if teal spare is seated in socket 3 (depth >= 16 mm, lateral error <= 1.5 mm, angle error <= 10.0 deg), failed module is not in any socket, and all healthy modules are seated; 1.00 if additionally DIAG is held >= 3 s showing steady green lamp, all four sockets seated, both grippers open, and all objects still (linear speed <= 5 mm/s, angular <= 0.2 rad/s) held continuously for 1.0 s (20 control steps). Zero-gate: any healthy module removed from socket for > 1 s (20 control steps) and not re-seated by end, fixture displacement > 5.0 mm, fixture tilt > 5.0 deg, or any module dropped off table (> 20 cm below table plane) permanently scores 0.0.
metadata.reset_notes: Return the original grey module to socket 3 and return the teal spare to its staging spot (x = 38.0 cm, y = -15.0 cm). If any healthy modules were disturbed, return them to their marked sockets (1 to 4). Release the white DIAG button. No parts or materials are consumed.
metadata.fidelity: Servos, keyed sockets (1 mm clearance per side, spring plunger) and the DIAG pushbutton (8 mm travel, hard stop, soft 100 N/m spring chosen for soft arm compliance) are simulated physically. Bus strip, sockets and controller box form one rigid fixture. Status lamp blinks and verification color states are computed in code and teleported as visual markers.

metadata.title: Keep a cable clear of a hot plate
metadata.instruction: The red disc is a hot plate. Put the lamp cable's plug into the white holder in front of the grey socket box. Never let any part of the cable touch or pass over the red disc, and leave the cable lying on the table at least 5 cm from the disc's edge.
metadata.context: Cords resting on hobs, heaters and soldering stations melt and cause home and workshop fires; a household or workshop robot tidying cables must respect a keep-out zone for the whole cable body during the motion, not just put the plug where it was asked.
metadata.setup: Station table, positions in cm from the midpoint between the two arm bases projected onto the table (x forward away from the robot, y to the robot's left). Hot plate: red 120 mm diameter, 1 mm thick disc (3D-printed PLA or red vinyl, a cold stand-in for a hot plate) centred at x 30, y 0, lying flat on the table. Lamp base: white 3D-printed PLA cylinder, 90 mm diameter, 60 mm tall, centred at x 21, y 30, clamped to the table. Lamp cable: black 8 mm round PVC cord, 60 cm from the lamp base to the plug, leaving the right-hand (-y) side of the lamp base at x 21, y 25.5, glued/strain-relieved into the base; it lies straight towards the right (-y) along x 21, so its surface is about 2.6 cm from the near edge of the red disc; its free end ends at x 21, y -34.5. Plug: black 3D-printed PLA box 35 x 16 x 12 mm (long side along the cable), epoxied on the cable end, 10 g. Plug holder: white 3D-printed PLA U-slot, inner floor 45 mm long (x) x 24 mm wide (y), side walls 4 mm thick and 8 mm tall, open towards the robot (-x end) and closed at the far end by the socket box; slot centre at x 30, y -24. Socket box: grey 60 x 90 x 50 mm box (e.g. a surface-mount electrical box), its robot-facing side at x 32.25, centred at y -24. Lamp base, disc, holder and socket box are fixed to the table.
metadata.scoring: Score 0 if at any moment of the trial any part of the cable or plug is over the red disc in top view (touching it, lying on it, or held in the air above it), judged from the top-camera video. This counts for the whole trial: putting the cable back where it started afterwards does not undo it. Also 0 unless at the end both grippers have let go (released = both gripper centres, between the finger pads, at least 3 cm from the plug centre and from every part of the cable). Otherwise, with the plug seated in the holder (plug inside the slot, lying on its floor, at most 4 mm above lying flat, sticking out of the open end by at most 1 cm) and released: 1.0 if the whole cable lies on the table (nowhere more than 2 cm above it) and every part of it is at least 5 cm from the disc's edge (tape measure, horizontal distance from the disc edge to the cable surface); 0.7 if every part is at least 3.5 cm from the disc's edge but the 1.0 condition does not hold; 0.4 if some part is closer than 3.5 cm. Plug not seated (also a plug held or resting near the slot) = 0. Success (1.0) when the full condition holds for 1 s with the cable at rest.
metadata.reset_notes: Lay the cable straight from the lamp base towards the right along x 21 cm (tape marks at y 25.5 and y -34.5 cm), plug at the right end with its long side along the cable and lying flat; remove anything from the slot. Check the red disc and holder are at their tape marks.
metadata.fidelity: Cable is 30 rigid 2 cm capsule segments with bending springs, no twist, no plasticity; plug is a rigid box welded to the last segment; the lamp-base end is welded to the world. The hot plate is a 1 mm thin fixed red cylinder with no heat; contact with it is judged geometrically (top-view overlap). Lamp base, holder and socket box are fixed rigid boxes/cylinders. The holder has no retention latch: the plug only has to lie in the slot.

metadata.title: Connect a robot's sensor cable: hold the loose proximity sensor still while turning the M12 coupling ring tight
metadata.instruction: Connect the robot's sensor cable to the new proximity sensor: pull the red protective cap off the sensor's connector and drop it in the blue parts tray; take the cable's connector off its parking holder and push it onto the sensor's connector; the sensor turns in its bracket because its nuts are not tightened yet, so hold the sensor still with one hand while the other turns the connector's knurled coupling ring until it is tight and the sensor's green light comes on. Then let go of both and take both arms back to where they started.
metadata.context: Robot cells are wired with M12 screw connectors; a technician connecting a newly fitted sensor holds the sensor still, because the coupling ring's thread drags a sensor whose mounting nuts are still loose round with it.
metadata.setup: A table in front of two arms (bases 61 cm apart), seen by one overhead camera and a camera on each wrist. Distances are measured forward from the line between the arm bases and sideways from the midpoint between them. (1) An aluminium fixture plate 1 cm thick, from 19 to 55 cm forward and from 20 cm right to 12 cm left of the centre line, fixed. (2) On it an anodised aluminium angle bracket whose 6 mm plate (5 cm wide) holds the sensor, fixed. (3) A steel inductive proximity sensor (0.13 kg): an M30 threaded stainless-steel barrel 3 cm across and 7 cm long with an orange plastic sensing face, two nickel-plated jam nuts (34 mm across flats) either side of the bracket's plate, and a grey plastic back end with a power light ring and a brass M12 male connector; its axis points 30 degrees down and to the left, at a machined aluminium part (5 x 4 x 3 cm, 0.15 kg, loose) in a blue nest at 30 cm forward, 8 cm left; its back end's face is 30 cm forward, 3 cm right of the centre line and 10.5 cm above the table. The jam nuts are loose: the sensor turns freely about its axis in the bracket. (4) A red rubber protective cap (1.9 cm across, 1.4 cm long, 8 g) on the sensor's connector. (5) The robot's orange PUR sensor cable, 5.5 mm thick, coming out of a grey cable duct (33 to 55 cm forward, 15 cm right, fixed) and ending, 19 cm on, in an M12 connector (28 g): a black moulded body 1.6 cm across with a knurled nickel-plated brass coupling ring 2.1 cm across and 1.6 cm long. It is parked on a black parking receptacle with a dummy thread, on a post at 23.5 cm forward, 3 cm right, at the same height and angle as the sensor. (6) A blue plastic parts tray, 6 cm square inside and 1.8 cm deep, at 24 cm forward, 12.5 cm right, fixed. (7) An orange robot arm parked behind the station (its base 66 cm forward, 15 cm right), fixed. The layout is the same in every trial, as in the screenshot.
metadata.scoring: Judged at the end. The connector is on (its thread has caught) once its front sits within 4 mm of the sensor's back end along the axis, within 3 mm of the axis and within 15 degrees of it; from then on it stays on the sensor's axis. While it is on, only the coupling ring's turn against the sensor (clockwise seen from behind) screws it on; the ring drags a sensor nobody holds round with it (a spring toward the ring's turn, at most 5 degrees behind). It is tight after one full turn against the sensor, and then the sensor's green light comes on; turned back 0.6 turns, it comes off. 1.0: the cap lies in the blue tray, the connector is on and tight, both hands have let go (each gripper's fingertip centre at least 4 cm from the coupling ring and from where the barrel is held) and both arms are back where they started (each within 5 cm); 0.5: the connector is on and tight; 0.25: the connector is on; else 0.0. The trial ends at the run limit, or once the full score has held for 1 s with the connector, sensor and cap still.
metadata.reset_notes: Unscrew the connector and park it on its parking receptacle, put the red cap back on the sensor's connector, and turn the sensor back so its yellow light faces up.
metadata.fidelity: Rigid-body simulation (Isaac Sim 6.1, PhysX, 20 Hz control). Simplified: the thread's friction on a loose sensor is a spring (at most 0.03 N m) turning the sensor with the ring; once on, a joint keeps the connector on the axis; one turn makes it tight (a real M12 takes about four); the moulded body turns with the ring. The cable is three stiff segments on damped ball joints. The plate, bracket, receptacle, duct, tray and robot are fixed. Cameras 1280 x 704 (Dream-1 sees 320 x 176).

metadata.title: Open a bottle with a detented safety loop and rocker latch
metadata.instruction: Open the bottle and keep it upright on the table.
metadata.context: Opening a reusable spill-resistant bottle requires stabilizing a free object while manipulating two independent mechanical restraints. This tests everyday assistive manipulation rather than unscrewing a cap or lifting an unconstrained lid.
metadata.setup: One empty grey steel-bodied bottle, 72 mm body diameter and approximately 282 mm closed height, in the official calibrated YAM station. Its free body is 350 g, spring-opening lid 25 g, spring-return rocker 7 g and U-shaped safety loop 6 g. Loop crown centreline diameter is 30 mm and section diameter 6 mm; rocker face diameter is 13 mm. Nominal bottle-base pose is (0.20,0,0.7480) m, upright, button facing -Y, lid closed and safety loop raised. Gravity settles it onto the 1.10 x 1.30 x 0.06 m table, whose centre is (0.36,0,0.7175) m and top is Z=0.7475 m. The two six-axis YAM arms stand at (0,0.305,0.75) m and (0,-0.305,0.75) m, with standard parallel grippers (0-93.9 mm jaw gap). Both start at joints [0,1,1,-0.6,0,0] radians and open grippers. The official station provides room, camera stand, top and wrist cameras, lights and robot meshes; their pinned source and the procedural bottle geometry reproduce the setup. Object jitter is zero. There are no additional task objects, holding fixtures, contents or tools.
metadata.scoring: Evaluate at 20 Hz. The current score at termination counts. Each condition requires 8 consecutive control ticks (0.4 s): 1.0 if lid angle >60 degrees from closed; otherwise 0.5 if lid >15 degrees; otherwise 0.25 if safety-loop angle >=150 degrees from raised; otherwise 0. A sampled bottle-axis dot world-up <=0.90 (tilt >=25.842 degrees), bottle-base origin Z<0.7375 m (10 mm below tabletop), or geometric table support lost (the 36 mm-radius bottom disc's lowest edge must stay within 10 mm of tabletop Z=0.7475 m, with base centre X in [-0.154,0.874] m and Y in [-0.614,0.614] m), nonfinite robot/bottle state, unavailable/nonfinite wrist measurement, or wrist joint reaction force norm >100 N for 4 consecutive ticks permanently invalidates the trial and overrides credit with zero. Use the larger of the two gripper incoming-joint force norms, including gravity. Full score or invalidation ends the episode; timeout receives the current partial score. Only robot contact may manipulate the bottle; direct bottle-joint actuation, pose edits, destruction or geometry edits are outside the allowed action interface.
metadata.run_limit: 2,400 control steps (120 simulated seconds at 20 Hz); PhysX integration is 0.001 s, 50 physics substeps per control tick.
metadata.reset_notes: Load yam/task.py in the official yam_arena station with object_jitter=0 and control_hz=20. Reset root/joint states to the fixed nominal setup and YAM READY pose with open jaws; passive mechanism forces operate during 10 unscored settling ticks (0.5 s). Refresh cameras and clear time, scorer counters and invalidation history. Official CLI verification uses seed 0; no task object randomization or consumables.
metadata.fidelity: Approximate USD/PhysX: four links, three passive joints and contact-only hooks/loop. Lid/rocker springs and an effective loop detent with COM gravity compensation run at 1 kHz. Mass, friction and springs are estimates; native dry friction/full dynamic bias are omitted. No fluids, seal compression, deformation or breakage. Wrist reactions have static-load checks only, not dynamic/hardware calibration. Table support is geometric. Further limits are in README.
metadata.scores: Dream-1 (dreamlabs/dream-1-beta, continuous session, 4 rows/request): 0.0 at 2400 steps / 120 s; scripted YAM demo: 1.0 at 405 steps / 20.25 s.

metadata.title: Snap a module onto a DIN rail
metadata.instruction: Pick up the blue module, hook the top of its back over the upper edge of the metal rail on the panel, swing its bottom in against the rail and push it until its latch clicks onto the rail.
metadata.context: Electricians and control-panel builders mount breakers, relays and terminals on DIN rails all day (O*NET 47-2111.00, 51-2022.00), and factories are trying to automate it. Unlike pushing a part straight in, the module must be hooked over the rail's upper lip, swung in about that hook and pushed until its spring latch snaps behind the lower lip.
metadata.setup: Positions in cm from the midpoint between the two arm bases, on the table (x forward, y left). Rail: a steel TS35 x 7.5 top-hat DIN rail, 22 cm long, running left to right, its centre 6 cm above the table at y -13, the front face of its lips at x 30; it is screwed to a fixed light grey panel (1 cm thick, 28 cm wide from y -27 to y 1, 9.5 cm tall from the table). A dark end clamp (1 cm wide, 5 cm tall, standing 1.2 cm proud of the rail) closes each end of the rail. Module: a blue 22.5 mm DIN-rail housing (PLA, 22.5 x 55 x 90 mm, 80 g) with a fixed hook at the top of its back, whose tooth drops 3.5 mm behind the rail's upper lip, and an orange spring latch at the bottom of its back (0.8 N per mm, 4 mm travel), whose tooth, chamfered at 45 degrees on its upper face toward the rail, reaches 1.5 mm behind the lower lip. It stands upright with its housing centre at x 19, y -21, back toward the panel, turned 25 degrees clockwise seen from above, between two fixed dark blocks (6.5 x 0.8 x 1.2 cm) 1 mm clear of either side of its base.
metadata.scoring: Measured at the end with a ruler and a photo. 1.0 if the module is mounted: hooked over the rail's upper lip, its back within 1.5 mm of the upper lip and 1 mm of the lower lip, square to the rail within 3 degrees, latch sprung back behind the lower lip, between the end clamps, and still (moving less than 1 mm over 1 s), for 1 s; 0.75 if, after hanging on its hook, its bottom was pushed to within 2 mm of the lower lip; 0.5 if, after being lifted, it hung on the rail by its hook (hook tooth behind the upper lip); 0.25 if it was lifted 3 cm; else 0.
metadata.reset_notes: Pull the latch down (its tab, with a screwdriver), tip the module's bottom out and lift it off the rail; stand it upright in its holder, back toward the panel at the marked angle.
metadata.fidelity: Rigid bodies built from boxes; rail, end clamps, panel and holder are fixed. The hook, rail lips and the latch's chamfered tooth are real colliders, so the latch clicks from contact alone; it is a prismatic joint with a spring drive and no preload. The rail's lips are 2 mm thick (1 mm on a real rail). Contact offsets are 0.5 mm, with light angular damping on the module. No contact force cap is enforced in simulation.

metadata.title: Release a two-latch lid and lift it out with both hands
metadata.instruction: Grip the two orange tabs on the blue lid, slide both toward the middle of the lid at the same time to release the latches, lift the lid out of the grey case, and set it down flat on the table to the right of the case.
metadata.context: Equipment covers, battery bays and storage cases often use a latch at each end that must be held open at the same time to lift the lid out; one latch alone leaves the lid locked in place (O*NET 49-2094.00, 49-9071.00).
metadata.setup: Positions in cm from the midpoint between the two arm bases, on the table (x forward, y left). Case: grey PLA, 1.5 kg, 26 x 8 x 4 cm, open top, lying with its long side along x, centred at x 25, y 8. Inside, a blue PLA lid (25 x 7 x 0.6 cm, 120 g) rests on two ledges with its top 1.3 cm below the rim. A slide latch sits at each end of the lid: an orange tab (3 cm wide, 3 cm tall, 0.4 cm thick) stands on the lid 9.8 cm from its centre, and a 2 x 0.3 cm tongue from it reaches 0.4 cm into a slot in the case's end wall. Sliding a tab 0.6 cm toward the lid's centre against its spring (0.3 N per mm) pulls the tongue out of the wall.
metadata.scoring: Measured at the end with a ruler and a top photo. 0 if the case was at any point moved more than 3 cm. Otherwise: 1.0 if, after being lifted out, the lid lies flat on the table (underside within 5 mm of it, tilted under 10 degrees) with its centre at least 8 cm to the side of the case's centreline, still (moving less than 1 mm over 1 s), for 1 s; 0.75 if the lid was lifted with its underside 1 cm above the case's rim; 0.5 if both latches were released at once (each tab slid at least 4 mm in); 0.25 if one latch was released; else 0.
metadata.reset_notes: Put the lid back into the case, tabs up, and let both latches spring out into their slots; set the case on its marked outline.
metadata.fidelity: Rigid bodies built from boxes; each latch is a prismatic joint with a spring drive and no preload, and its tongue engages the wall slot by contact alone. The case is heavy (1.5 kg) so it stays put. Light angular damping is added to the parts. No contact force cap is enforced in simulation.

metadata.title: Push a peg home past a hidden obstruction without forcing it
metadata.instruction: Push the peg fully into the block.
metadata.context: A steel ball hidden at the end of the bore stops the peg 1.5 cm short. Nothing in the instruction or the cameras shows it; the only cue is the early stop. Pushing harder past an unexpected stop damages parts (a latching end stop trips above 3 N), so the robot should back off, find the cause, tip the ball out and then insert the peg, as with a dropped bearing ball or debris in a bore.
metadata.setup: Positions in cm from the midpoint between the two arm bases, on the table top (x forward, y left, z up). Arms start in the ready pose. Block: loose light wood (or PLA), 11 x 7 x 5.5 cm (y by x by z), 0.20 kg, centred at x 31, y 4, long side along y (left-right). A square blind bore 2.4 x 2.4 cm, 9 cm deep, runs along y from the block's right (-y) end face, at y -1.5; its axis is 2.75 cm above the table. The bore's closed end is a latching end stop that trips at 3 N (see README). Peg: a 20 mm round wooden dowel 8.5 cm long, painted blue, glued into a square 4 x 3.4 x 3.4 cm dark-brown wooden head, 50 g, lying in the bore with 4 cm of shaft inside (head toward the right arm, 4.5 cm from the end face); it rests drooping slightly in the clearance. Ball: a 20 mm steel ball bearing, 33 g, at the closed end of the bore, not visible from outside. Tray: an empty grey plastic parts tray, 14 x 14 cm, 1.5 cm rims, 0.15 kg, loose, centred at x 25, y 18. Nothing else on the table. Mark the block's and tray's outlines with tape.
metadata.scoring: From a ruler, a photo and the video. 0 if the end stop's latch tripped (peg forced onto the ball, over 3 N for 12.5 ms), or the block, peg or ball fell off the table. Otherwise, with the ball out of the block (anywhere on the table): 1.0 if the peg's head is within 3 mm of the end face (success, held 1 s); 0.5 if at least 4 cm of shaft is in the bore; 0.25 otherwise. Ball in the block: 0. The peg counts only with its tip within 1 cm of the bore axis.
metadata.reset_notes: Push the end stop's indicator pin back flush, put the ball back at the bore's end, slide the peg in 4 cm (head 4.5 cm from the end face), empty the tray, and set block and tray in their taped outlines.
metadata.fidelity: Approximate. Rigid primitives: box block and tray, round peg (cylinder collider) in a square bore, sphere ball, which stops the peg by contact. Damage: PhysX peg-ball force over 3 N for 12.5 ms; the real end stop moves 3 mm when it trips. The demo's push peaks at 0.2 N, a 10 cm over-push at 13 N. No rolling resistance. Details in README.

metadata.title: Hold a sprung-up M.2 drive flat in its socket with one hand while the other turns the latch over its end
metadata.instruction: Hold the M.2 drive down flat in its socket with one hand while the other turns the latch's knob a quarter turn counterclockwise so its arm holds the drive's end down, then let go with both hands.
metadata.context: Building and servicing computers and servers includes fitting M.2 drives. A drive goes into its socket at an angle and springs up, so a technician holds it flat with one hand while the other fastens its end; many motherboards use a tool-less quarter-turn latch on the standoff instead of a screw.
metadata.setup: A table in front of two arms (bases 61 cm apart), seen by one overhead camera and a camera on each wrist. Distances are measured forward from the line between the arm bases and sideways from the midpoint between them. (1) A fixed green motherboard, 18 x 22 cm and 1.2 cm thick, centred 28 cm forward and 3.5 cm left, with low memory slots, a CPU socket and chips on it. (2) Its M.2 socket, 28 cm forward and 9 cm left, holding a loose M.2 drive (22 x 110 mm, 8 g: a black board with chips and a white label) that points right along the left-right line, sprung up 20 degrees from flat (its far end 3.8 cm up). (3) At the drive's far end, 1.75 cm right of the centre line, a standoff with a quarter-turn latch: an arm 13 mm long just over where the flat drive's top would be, pointing right (off the drive's end) at the start, and a black stem 6 mm across and 4 cm tall topped by a black knob 14 mm across and 12 mm tall. The layout is the same in every trial, as in the screenshot.
metadata.scoring: Judged at the end of the trial. Flat: the drive within 2.5 degrees of flat in its socket. Latched: flat, with the latch turned at least 70 degrees counterclockwise (seen from above) from its start, its arm over the drive's end. Let go: both grippers' fingertip centres (TCPs) at least 3 cm from the drive and from the latch's knob. 1.0: latched and both let go; 0.5: latched; 0.25: the drive held flat for 1 s at some point; else 0.0. The trial ends at the run limit, or once the full score has held with the drive and latch still for 1 s.
metadata.reset_notes: Turn the latch back so its arm points right, off the drive's end, and let the drive spring back up 20 degrees in its socket.
metadata.fidelity: Rigid-body simulation (Isaac Sim 6.1, PhysX, 20 Hz control). Simplified: the drive's spring is a hinge spring at the socket (0.03 N m holding it 20 degrees up, 0.09 N m pressed flat); the latch is a damped hinge on its standoff with a stop at a quarter turn; no electrical contact. The latch's knob stands on a 4 cm stem, taller than real ones, so a gripper fits on it. The motherboard is fixed. Cameras 1280 x 704 (Dream-1 sees 320 x 176).

metadata.title: Straighten and hold a newborn training doll's two sprung legs flat while the other arm closes the footboard
metadata.instruction: Measure the training doll's length on the white length board, leaving the blue footboard at the reading, then let go.
metadata.context: Paediatric nurses (O*NET 29-1141), medical assistants (31-9092) and community health workers (21-1094) measure infants' recumbent length on a length board at well-baby and growth-monitoring visits. The skill is straightening an infant's two sprung legs and holding them flat: a newborn's legs spring back into flexion, so in the WHO method one hand holds both knees flat while the other slides the footpiece to the heels. Training doll, 45 cm.
metadata.setup: Station table; positions in cm from the midpoint between the two arm bases, x forward, y to the robot's left; heights above the table top. (1) Infant length board, fixed to the table: white (0.95, 0.95, 0.93) melamine-faced plywood plank 68 x 26 x 1.8 cm, about 2 kg, smooth laminate top with friction 0.35 static / 0.30 dynamic, centred at (20, 10), spanning x 7 to 33 and y -24 to 44. A fixed white plywood headpiece 26 x 1.5 x 16 cm stands on its +y end with its face at y 42.5 (the 0 mm mark). A yellow (0.95, 0.80, 0.15) printed tape 2 cm wide runs along x 31 from 0 mm at y 42.5 to 600 mm at y -17.5, with black (0.05, 0.05, 0.05) ticks every 50 mm. (2) Footboard: blue (0.15, 0.35, 0.85) painted plywood plate 20 x 1.2 x 16 cm on a 20 x 6 x 0.8 cm shoe riding in the board's rail, with a beech (0.80, 0.62, 0.40) handle 2.2 x 5 x 2.2 cm sticking 5 cm out of its back, 12 cm above the board; 0.30 kg in all; it slides along y with 1.5 N static (1.2 N moving) rail friction; its face starts at y -9.5, the 520 mm mark. (3) Newborn length-measurement training doll fitted with torsion-spring hip and knee hinges: vinyl, 45 cm crown to sole, 0.45 kg, skin colour (0.93, 0.78, 0.66), friction 0.6 / 0.5 (shins and feet smooth glossy vinyl, 0.25 / 0.2), lying face up along y with its midline on x 20 and its crown at y 42.4, 1 mm from the headpiece. Head (10 cm round), trunk (10 x 15 x 6.2 cm), arms and a white (0.97, 0.97, 0.97) cloth nappy are one rigid 0.33 kg body. Legs at x 17.4 and 22.6: thighs 3.8 cm thick and 8.5 cm hip to knee (35 g each); shins with feet 8 cm knee to sole (25 g each), feet 3.2 x 2 x 7 cm with the toes up. The hips (at y 13.9, 1.9 cm above the board) and knees are sprung hinges about x: hips 0.07 N m/rad toward 95 deg of flexion, knees 0.05 N m/rad toward 81 deg. At rest the legs are drawn up at hips 80 deg and knees 95 deg with the feet in the air, and the soles reach only the 391 mm mark; with every joint straight the soles are 45.0 cm from the crown.
metadata.scoring: Whole-run record (a linkkit History updated every control step and cleared only by the simulator reset) of the hip and knee angles, the crown-to-headpiece gap, each sole's gap to the footboard face, the footboard reading (headpiece face to footboard face) and its speed, the doll's lowest point and trunk position, and each gripper's pad clearance and speed. Touch = both hips at most 12 deg and both knees at most 15 deg, the crown within 2 mm of the headpiece, both soles within 2 mm of the footboard face and in front of it, and the footboard slower than 5 mm/s. Measured = a touch held for 0.5 s at any time. Gates, any time in the run, each gives 0: the doll's lowest point more than 20 mm above the board; the trunk pushed off the board. Ladder at the end of the episode: both legs held straight with the crown on the headpiece for 1 s = 0.25; measured = 0.5; measured and the footboard at the end within 5 mm of a reading taken during the measured touch (within the touch limits a touch reads about 445 to 460 mm on the 450 mm doll) = 0.75; and for the last 1 s every pad of both grippers at least 30 mm from the doll and the footboard with both grippers slower than 5 mm/s = 1.0 (success, which must also hold 1 s). Moving the legs or the footboard back never clears a gate or a measurement. Doing nothing scores 0. Real trial: read the footboard face against the tape on a top photo (to 5 mm); a side photo during the hold shows both knees flat, the crown on the headpiece and both soles on the footboard.
metadata.reset_notes: Nothing is consumed and the board is fixed. Lay the doll face up on its tape outline, midline on the board's centre line (x 20 cm), crown 1 mm from the headpiece, and let the legs spring up to rest (hips about 80 deg, knees about 95 deg, feet in the air). Slide the footboard to the 520 mm mark (face at y -9.5 cm). object_jitter=0.
metadata.fidelity: Rigid links: a 45 cm, 0.45 kg vinyl training doll (a real newborn is about 3.3 kg) whose hip and knee springs (0.07, 0.05 N m/rad) stand in for newborn flexion tone. Hips flex in one plane and the ankles are fixed at 90 deg. The doll does not wriggle; the fixed headpiece stands in for the assistant who holds the head. Shins and feet are slick vinyl (0.25 on the 0.35 laminate) so the heels slide. The footboard slides on a joint with 1.5 N friction; the reading comes from that joint.

metadata.title: Lift a cable so a cart can pass
metadata.instruction: Get the blue cart past the orange finish marks without it ever touching the black power cord: lift the cord with one arm and slide the cart under it with the other. Keep the cart on the table. Then lay the cord back down along its line and let go of it.
metadata.context: Rolling a cart over a floor cord can crush its jacket. OSHA 29 CFR 1910.334(a)(1): "Portable equipment shall be handled in a manner which will not cause damage"; (a)(2)(i) lists "pinched or crushed outer jacket" as a sign of damage to look for. So the cord is lifted clear and the cart rolled under it, then the cord is laid back flat. One hand must hold a deformable cord high enough while the other moves a load under it without contact.
metadata.setup: Station table; cm from the midpoint between the arm bases (x forward, y left). Black 8 mm PVC cord lies straight along y at x 28 from a grey floor cord retractor (5x4x3 cm box, cord exit y -20) to a yellow wall cord reel (8x6x6 cm, slot y 38); each spring retractor pays out up to 12 cm (0.3 N rest pull, ~1 N at 12 cm). White inline switch box on the cord, 50x30x22 mm, 25 g, y -2 to +3. Grey partition 22x1.2x7 cm, x 18-40, centred y 27, with an 18 mm wide, 20 mm tall notch at x 28 at its base; the cord passes it. Cart: light blue wooden block 14x5x3 cm, 200 g, centre x 18, y 12, long side along x (front 2.4 cm before the cord). Finish line x 34: two orange tape marks 1x2 cm at y 7 and y 17.
metadata.scoring: The cart must pass under the cord: when its centre crosses the cord line x 28 (either way) it is within 5 cm of y 12 and the cord's underside over the cart's width plus 1 cm each side is at or above the cart top (3 cm up). Score 0 if at any time (latched): a crossing fails this; the cart comes within 2 mm of the cord or switch box, rises over 1 cm or tilts over 15 deg. At the end: never passed under, or cart not fully past the finish line (rear edge beyond x 34, centre within 5 cm of y 12, upright) = 0; cart past, cord not back or still held = 0.7; cart past, cord between retractor and partition on the table (centre 1.5 cm up at most) within 3 cm of x 28, grippers 3 cm or more from all of the cord = 1.0.
metadata.reset_notes: Let the cord go so both retractors pull it straight along the x 28 tape line, switch box between its y -2 and +3 marks. Slide the cart back to its tape outline (x 11-25, y 9.5-14.5).
metadata.fidelity: Cord: rigid 2 cm segments with bending springs, no twist; switch box rigid. Retractors are modelled as linear springs (6 N/m, 5 cm preload, 12 cm hard stop) on the cord ends; a real spring cord reel gives a similar 0.3-1 N pull. Cart is a sliding block (no wheels, friction 0.5-0.8): real trial uses a block or a free-rolling toy cart. Touch is judged geometrically (gap at most 2 mm) each 50 ms step.

metadata.title: Hold a stick umbrella by its handle with one hand while the other pushes the runner up until it latches open
metadata.instruction: Hold the umbrella by its handle with one hand, and with the other push the runner up the shaft toward the tip until it latches and the umbrella is open; then let go of the runner, move that hand out of the way, and lift the open umbrella up by its handle, tip raised.
metadata.context: Opening a stick umbrella is an everyday two-handed action: one hand holds the handle while the other pushes the runner up the shaft against the ribs' springs until it clicks into its latch. A robot helping at home or in a shop doorway meets this and many similar spring-loaded catches.
metadata.setup: A table in front of two arms (bases 61 cm apart), seen by one overhead camera and a camera on each wrist. Distances are measured forward from the line between the arm bases and sideways from the midpoint between them. (1) A fixed dark-grey painted steel stand: two cradles under the umbrella's shaft, 19 cm right and 4 cm left of the centre line; the handle is free. (2) A loose stick umbrella, 220 g, closed, lying on the stand along the left-right line 28 cm forward, its shaft 14.5 cm above the table: its tip 33 cm right of the centre line, a steel shaft 40 cm long and a wooden handle 10 cm long and 3 cm across, from 7 to 17 cm left of the centre line. Its navy nylon canopy (eight panels on 14 cm steel ribs) is furled along the shaft by the tip. (3) The runner, a dark plastic (nylon) sleeve 2.4 cm across and 3 cm long on the shaft, 3 cm right of the centre line; pushed 12 cm toward the tip it opens the ribs and latches. The layout is the same in every trial, as in the screenshot.
metadata.scoring: Judged at the end of the trial. Travel: how far the runner has been pushed from closed toward the tip, of its 12 cm; the ribs open as it goes (60 degrees from the shaft at the top). At 95% it latches and stays. Let go: both grippers' fingertip centres (TCPs) at least 3 cm from the runner. Held up: the umbrella's tip at least 12 cm above where it lay, with a TCP within 4 cm of the handle's axis (held by its handle). 1.0: latched, let go, and held up by the handle; 0.5: latched; 0.25: pushed at least half way at some point; else 0.0. The trial ends at the run limit, or once the full score has held for 1 s with the umbrella held still.
metadata.reset_notes: Release the latch, let the runner slide back to closed, furl the canopy and lay the umbrella back on its stand.
metadata.fidelity: Rigid-body simulation (Isaac Sim 6.1, PhysX, 20 Hz control). Simplified: the canopy is eight rigid panels whose angle the task file sets from the runner's travel each step (no stretchers or fabric); they do not collide. The ribs' springs are one spring on the runner (1.2 N to start, 6 N at the top), and the latch is a stop the task file sets at the top. The stand is fixed. Cameras 1280 x 704 (Dream-1 sees 320 x 176).

metadata.title: Plug both ends of a patch cord into a cable tester
metadata.instruction: Connect the loose patch cord to the cable tester for certification: push one plug fully into the jack of the main unit (blue, left) and the other plug fully into the jack of the remote unit (orange, right), without pulling the first plug out, then let go of both plugs.
metadata.context: Telecom and network cable installers (O*NET 49-9052, 49-2022) certify each patch cord by seating its two ends in a tester's main and remote units. The cord is short, so both ends must be brought over together and the second seated without unseating the first.
metadata.setup: Positions in cm from the midpoint between the arm bases (x forward, y left); fixed parts taped down. Main unit: blue PLA box 8 (x) x 7 (y) x 4 cm tall, centre x 36, y +28. Its jack: dark grey PLA sleeve 28 mm wide x 20.5 mm tall x 40 mm long on the unit's right face, opening (20 x 16.5 mm, 26 mm deep, at table level, centre x 36) at y +20.5, facing right. Remote unit: same, orange, mirrored at y -28, jack opening at y -20.5 facing left. Cord: grey 6 mm round PVC cord, 40 cm, straight along x 22 from y +20 to -20; on each end a dark grey PLA plug body 55 x 16 x 14 mm, 15 g, lying flat, pointing at its unit.
metadata.scoring: Score 0 if: at the end a gripper still holds or touches either plug (sim: a gripper centre within 4.5 cm of a plug centre); a tester unit was moved. Otherwise, at the end: 0.5 for each jack (main, remote) holding a plug whose front end is at least 15 mm inside the jack opening (mark on each plug 15 mm from its front end must be hidden in the jack). A plug on top of, beside or in front of a jack, or in less than 15 mm, earns nothing. Either plug may go in either unit. Both jacks = 1.0.
metadata.reset_notes: Pull both plugs out, lay the cord straight along the x 22 cm tape line from y +20 to y -20 cm with the plugs lying flat on their 16 mm side, each pointing at its unit. The units stay taped at their marks.
metadata.fidelity: Cord: 20 rigid 2 cm segments with bending springs (no twist, stretch, plasticity). Plugs: rigid boxes with no latch or contacts, held in the jack only by its walls and friction, so the cord can tug a seated plug out with little force; the real trial uses the same latchless plug bodies, and seating is judged by insertion depth. Jack clearance is 2 mm per side (real RJ45/LC fit is tighter). Units are fixed (taped down in real trials).

metadata.title: Release a push-fit fitting and pull the pipe out
metadata.instruction: Press the orange release collet on the brass fitting in and hold it there while you pull the copper pipe out of the fitting, then lay the pipe down flat on the table.
metadata.context: Plumbers and heating technicians (O*NET 47-2152.00, 49-9021.00) take pipes out of push-fit fittings when re-routing or replacing a section: the fitting's grab ring bites the pipe, so the release collet has to be pressed in and held while the pipe is pulled out. One hand holds the collet, the other pulls.
metadata.setup: Positions in cm from the midpoint between the two arm bases, on the table (x forward, y left). A grey base plate (9 x 14.7 x 0.8 cm) lies at x 23.5 to 32.5, y 1.5 to 16.2, held by four dark cleats 2 cm tall screwed to the table; a white wall plate (12 x 1.2 x 11 cm) stands on its far end at y 15 to 16.2. A 15 mm copper stub comes out of the wall along -y into a brass push-fit coupling (3 x 3 x 8 cm, axis 4.5 cm above the table at x 28) on a grey pedestal; the coupling's open mouth faces -y at y 2. The base, wall, stub and coupling weigh 5 kg together. An orange release collet (a square ring 5 cm wide, 3.6 cm tall, 0.5 cm thick, with a 2 cm hole) sits 0.4 cm in front of the mouth; a spring (0.4 N per mm) holds it out and it presses in 3.5 mm. A loose 15 mm copper pipe, 30 cm long, 84 g, lies along y with its end pushed 2.5 cm into the coupling (to y 4.5) and its far end (y -25.5) resting on a wooden block (3 x 2 x 3.7 cm) at y -23.5. A grab tooth inside the coupling holds the pipe in unless the collet is pressed at least 2.5 mm.
metadata.scoring: Measured with a ruler. 0 if the fitting was at any point moved more than 5 mm. 1.0 if the pipe, after being pulled out, lies flat on the table (axis level within 10 degrees, resting on the table) with every point at least 4 cm from the coupling's mouth, and is still for 1 s; 0.75 if, after the collet was pressed, the pipe's end came at least 5 mm out of the mouth (pulled 3 cm); 0.5 if, after the collet was pressed, the pipe was pulled 5 mm; 0.25 if the collet was pressed 2.5 mm; else 0.
metadata.reset_notes: Press the collet and push the pipe back into the coupling to its stop (2.5 cm in), let the collet go so the tooth bites, and rest the pipe's far end on the block.
metadata.fidelity: Rigid bodies built from boxes and cylinders. The grab ring is one tooth on a stiff slider that drops into a 3 mm groove in the pipe (a real ring's teeth bite plain pipe); while the collet, a spring slider, is pressed 2.5 mm, the task lifts the tooth, standing in for the collet's cone. The bore is square with 1.5 mm play and no O-ring. The fitting assembly is held by cleats. No contact force cap is enforced in simulation.

metadata.title: Reseat the half-inserted plug
metadata.instruction: One of the four patch cords plugged into the back of the switch is not fully seated. Find the loose plug and push it fully into its port without pulling or unseating any of the other plugs, then let go.
metadata.context: A half-seated cord is a classic cause of flapping links in a server rack; data-centre technicians (O*NET 49-2011.00, 15-1231.00) find it among neighbours by eye and reseat it without disturbing live links next to it.
metadata.setup: Table top is the reference (z = 0); x is measured forward from the line through the two arm bases, y to the left of the midline between them. Switch rear panel: white 3D-printed PLA block 60 mm (x) x 200 mm (y) x 44 mm tall (1U), occupying x 40.0-46.0 cm, y -10.0 to +10.0 cm, screwed to the table, its back face (x 40.0 cm) towards the robot. Four ports in that face, open at table level (floor = table), each 17.5 mm wide x 15.5 mm tall x 26 mm deep along +x, centred at y +6.75 (A), +2.25 (B), -2.25 (C), -6.75 cm (D). Four patch cords: 6 mm round PVC cord, 25 cm long, colours A blue, B yellow, C green, D red, each ending in a dark grey rigid plug body 55 (along the cord) x 16 x 14 mm tall, 15 g (3D-printed PLA, no latch: held in the port only by friction), lying on the table in line with its port. Seated plugs (A, C, D): tip 25 mm inside the port, plug rear end at x 37.0 cm, cord running straight back along x to its free end at x 12.0 cm. Loose plug (B, default; any port can be chosen): tip 8 mm inside, rear end at x 35.3 cm (sticks out 17 mm further), cord free end at x 10.3 cm. The cords' far ends are free on the table. All parts match the setup screenshot.
metadata.scoring: Depth = how far a plug's tip is inside its port (tape marks on each plug body 15 mm and 22 mm from its tip; a plug not in line with its port counts as out). Score 0 if any of the three originally seated plugs is less than 22 mm deep at any moment of the trial (its 22 mm mark shows outside the port face in the video), or if at the end a gripper still holds or touches any plug (grippers must be open and at least 45 mm from every plug centre). Otherwise, by the loose plug's depth at the end: at least 22 mm -> 1.0; 15 to 22 mm -> 0.5; less than 15 mm -> 0. Pressing already seated plugs home is allowed. Real trial: also 0 if the panel is moved (it cannot move in simulation).
metadata.reset_notes: Set the three seated plugs 25 mm deep (30 mm of body outside, 1 mm short of the port bottom), pull the loose plug back until only 8 mm is inside (47 mm outside, mark on the body), and lay each cord straight back towards the robot along its port's line. The panel is screwed down and needs no reset.
metadata.fidelity: Cords: chains of 2 cm rigid segments with bending springs (no twist, stretch or plasticity), far ends free. Plugs: rigid boxes welded to the cord ends, held in their ports only by the walls and friction (no latch, contacts or insertion force). Panel: fixed rigid boxes. Grippers rigid with PhysX friction.

metadata.title: Sort bottles safely in a crowded vertical rack
metadata.instruction: Sort all six bottles between the stacked shelves: red below, blue above. The gray staging pedestal is available. Keep every bottle upright and prevent falls, including neighboring bottles. Finish with both grippers open and withdrawn, with every bottle stable for two seconds.
metadata.context: Storage and return logistics often require correcting a mixed arrangement while preserving neighboring containers. Unlike removing one selected bottle to an empty tray, this task requires moving misplaced bottles between two constrained shelf levels and finishing with the whole rack correctly classified and stable.
metadata.setup: YAM station; wood table 1100x1300x60 mm. Wood rack: 2 shelves and roof 130x170x12 mm, back 12x194x320, 2 sides 130x12x370; gray wood stage 80x80x160. Six plastic bottles: height 100 mm, diameter 36 mm, mass 80 g. Shelf tops z=797.5/957.5 mm; bottles x=294, y=0,+/-60 mm. Lower row red/blue/red; upper blue/red/blue. Front margin 6 mm, neighbor gap 24 mm. Full inventory, materials, poses and station parts: scene_inventory.json and README.md.
metadata.scoring: Any bottle tilt>20deg, downward speed>0.35m/s, bottom z<0.7915m, top z>1.1775m, center x outside [0.07,0.44] or y outside [-0.15,0.27] m, or invalid pose: permanent 0. Sorted: whole bounding box on matching shelf, edge margin>=3mm, bottom within 4mm, tilt<=5deg. Credit needs 2s with all tilts<=5deg, center drift<=3mm from window start, jaws>=75% open, both TCPs>=85mm from every center. Score=max(0,sorted-4)/2: 0,0.5,1; initial 0. See PHYSICAL_SCORING.md.
metadata.reset_notes: Restore the six listed upright bottle poses, zero velocities, arms to READY, and a fresh safety latch. Fixtures remain fixed. Use seed 0 and zero pose jitter.
metadata.fidelity: PhysX rigid contact/gravity at 240 Hz; robot control and final stability samples at 20 Hz. Compound bottle colliders, fixed wood rack and real contact constraints; no snapping or attachments. Physical trials use colored plastic bottles. Glass fracture and material damage are outside scope. Force is telemetry only; vertical-axis spin is irrelevant. Pose-based safety is latched, with a two-second position-drift/release window. Calibrated-video measurement limits: PHYSICAL_SCORING.md.
metadata.scores: Dream-1 run: 0.0; scripted demo: 1.0. Both recorded under the finalized observable scorer.

metadata.title: Snap a circuit board out of its panel over the break edge
metadata.instruction: Separate the circuit board from its panel and tray it.
metadata.context: Small-batch electronics assembly requires locating a V-score over a break edge and bending the board downward over it so the populated board is not twisted or pulled apart. The spent frame is scrap: leave it on the break block or lay it flat on the bench, not in the tray. Done by: electrical and electronic equipment assemblers (O*NET 51-2022.00; https://www.onetonline.org/link/summary/51-2022.00).
metadata.setup: Station tabletop z=0.7475 m, spanning x -0.19 to 0.91 m, y -0.65 to 0.65 m; x forward, y left; arm bases (0,+/-0.305,0.75) m. All dimensions metres and all yaw zero. Fixed grey steel break block with a flush bonded conductive-rubber bench-mat facing (included in the stated top height): origin (0.205,0.085,0.7475), box local centre (0,0,0.020), size (0.130,0.170,0.040); 130 mm straight front edge along x at y=0 (x 0.140-0.270 m); the 80 mm score line is centred on it. Dynamic green FR-4 frame, 0.040 kg, root (0.205,0.025,0.7893): substrate box centre (0,0.073,0), size (0.080,0.146,0.0016); grey hollow conductive-plastic tooling rail represented by box (0,0.130,0.0088), size (0.080,0.032,0.016). Gold copper fiducial discs at (+/-0.028,0.023,0.00095), radius 0.003, height 0.0003; black ink tooling-hole marks at (+/-0.028,0.080,0.00095), radius 0.002, height 0.0003, all z-axis cylinders (marks, not holes). Dynamic green FR-4 board, 0.030 kg, root (0.205,-0.020,0.7893): substrate box (0,0,0), size (0.080,0.090,0.0016); blue plastic terminal housing (0,-0.005,0.0083), size (0.032,0.020,0.015); black plastic component boxes (-0.027,0.025,0.0048), size (0.012,0.014,0.008), and (+0.027,0.025,0.0038), size (0.012,0.014,0.006); gold copper score stripe (0,0.044,0.00095), size (0.076,0.001,0.0003). Fixed black conductive-rubber landing nest, origin (0.205,-0.048,0.7475): floor box (0,0,0.001), size (0.092,0.104,0.002); side lips (+/-0.045,0,0.003), size (0.004,0.104,0.002); front lip (0,-0.050,0.003), size (0.086,0.004,0.002). The block face closes the back, giving an 86 x 96 mm landing pocket. Fixed dark-grey conductive-plastic ESD tray, origin (0.205,-0.215,0.7475): floor box (0,0,0.002), size (0.140,0.144,0.004); side walls (+/-0.068,0,0.010), size (0.004,0.144,0.012); end walls (0,+/-0.070,0.010), size (0.132,0.004,0.012), clear opening 132 x 136 mm. All fixed items are bench-mounted. Friction static/dynamic: block and frame proxy 0.80/0.65 (representing dry conductive-rubber contact), board/nest/tray 0.60/0.45; contact offsets 0.0002 m, rest offsets zero, restitution zero. Board/frame joined at the V-score by a passive fixed joint, break torque 0.480 Nm and force 100 N. The two dynamic roots are never independently jittered.
metadata.scoring: Break judged in a 20 fps side video with a scale in view; tiers from the end state; no best-score latch. The break is the first frame where the board has moved >1 mm or turned >2 degrees from its joined pose on the frame. Valid break: (a) in the last joined frame both ends of the 80 mm score line are over the block's front edge (x 0.140-0.270 m), within 2 mm of it in y and of score height (z 0.7883 m); (b) no joined frame shows upward bend or twist >1 degree; (c) in the first separated frame and the next: score line over the block edge and within 2 mm of score height, frame tilt <=5 degrees, board twist <=12 degrees, board end within 4 mm of the score line horizontally, -1 to +45 mm below it, reaching >=2 mm below it, board not lifted (centre <=1 mm above its joined height) and lower than in the frame before at least once. Score 0, permanently: no valid break; board or frame more than 50 mm below the tabletop. 0 while the board is back within 1 mm and 2 degrees of its joined pose. Otherwise 0.5. 0.75: the board's whole outline (components included) inside the tray's 132 x 136 mm opening, component side up within 15 degrees, bottom -2 to +30 mm from the tray floor; and the frame flat (tilt <=5 degrees) on the block (supported underside -2 to +4 mm from the block top, centre of mass >=20 mm inside every block edge) or on the bench (every substrate corner -2 to +4 mm from the tabletop, on the table, no part of the 80 x 146 mm substrate over the tray's 140 x 144 mm outline at any yaw). 1.0: the 0.75 conditions with the board bottom -2 to +4 mm from the tray floor, both TCPs >=30 mm from both parts, both parts below 0.010 m/s and 0.15 rad/s for 1 s. A board or frame still held but inside the 0.75 limits earns 0.75; a flipped, on-rim or stacked board, or a frame outside the bands, earns 0.5.
metadata.reset_notes: At every reset, disable the joint, restore both bodies to their authored initial poses with zero velocities, restore the joined constraint frames and 0.480 Nm/100 N limits, and re-arm the joint before the 0.5 s settling period. The score line starts 25 mm behind the edge with 1 mm initial support clearance. Both bodies are dynamic, without independent starting jitter. Replace a real scored panel each trial and deburr or guard fractured edges for safe handling.
metadata.fidelity: Rigid FR-4 board/frame proxies and a passive 0.480 Nm/100 N joint approximate a V-scored web; no deformable fracture or component stress is modelled. Uniform collider density, marked tooling holes, solid rail envelope and fixed ESD nest/tray simplify construction. Friction represents dry conductive-rubber contact. Pose history checks downward separation, rejecting visible torsion, lifting and pulling. Closed pads slide, hold and bend; the joint is re-armed at every reset.

metadata.title: Close a snap-fit case lid
metadata.instruction: Put the blue lid into the pocket of the grey case with its orange tabs over the orange latches, then press the front edge of the lid down until both latches click.
metadata.context: Closing a snap-fit cover is the last step of countless electronics repairs and assembly jobs (O*NET 49-2094.00, 51-2028.00). The case is light and stands on a narrow foot, so pressing the latches tips it unless the other hand steadies it.
metadata.setup: Positions in cm from the midpoint between the two arm bases, on the table (x forward, y left). Case base: grey PLA box 12 x 7 x 2.5 cm, 150 g, standing on a fixed grey 4 x 5 x 2 cm block whose centre is at x 21, y -5; both turned 45 degrees clockwise seen from above, so the case's front end points forward and to the right. Its top has a pocket 11.6 x 6.6 cm and 0.75 cm deep (2 mm walls, the middle 6 cm of each long wall open). Two orange PLA latch plates, 1.2 x 1.2 cm, sit in the pocket 4.5 cm in front of the case centre and 2.2 cm either side of its midline, 4 mm above the pocket floor on springs (2.5 N per mm, 4 mm travel). Lid: blue PLA plate 11.4 x 6.4 x 0.75 cm, 40 g, with two orange 1.2 x 1.2 cm tabs on top over the latch positions, lying flat on two fixed grey 1.2 x 5 x 1.5 cm rails 8 cm apart centred at x 11, y 17, turned 30 degrees clockwise.
metadata.scoring: Measured at the end with a ruler and a top photo. 0 if the case base was at any point moved more than 3 cm or tilted more than 20 degrees. Otherwise: 1.0 if both latches have clicked (lid underside within 0.7 mm of the pocket floor above each latch) and the lid lies in the pocket (centre within 3 mm of the pocket centre, turned less than 5 degrees, tilted less than 10 degrees) let go (both grippers at least 3 cm from the lid) and still (moving less than 1 mm) over the last second, for 1 s; 0.75 if one latch clicked after the lid was placed; 0.5 if, after being lifted, the lid was set down at rest in the pocket; 0.25 if the lid was lifted 3 cm above its start; else 0.
metadata.reset_notes: Lift the lid out of the case (release the latches), lay it flat on the rails, ends centred on them, tabs up and pointing toward the case, and set the case on its foot in its marked outline.
metadata.fidelity: Rigid bodies built from boxes; the foot and rails are fixed. The latch plates are spring-loaded sliders, but the snap hook itself is not modelled: a latch clicks when the lid's underside comes within 0.7 mm of the pocket floor above it, and once both have clicked the lid is held seated relative to the case, rewritten every control step. No contact force cap is enforced in simulation.

metadata.title: Fit a split cable guide and verify drawer travel
metadata.instruction: Fit a split guide around the cable at the panel opening and lock it with the orange keeper. Keep both plugs seated throughout. Withdraw both hands, then press the yellow release and let the drawer open to the marked line on its own.
metadata.context: A service drawer's connected wiring needs a guide that protects it at the panel opening and leaves clearance for its thicker sleeve during travel.
metadata.setup: Calibrated YAM bench. Aluminium panel and 50 mm spring drawer, 8 mm PVC cable with a 12 mm sleeve, two dummy plugs seated in fixed and drawer sockets. Two PETG guide inserts with 10 and 16 mm openings start on the left. Orange keeper starts open, yellow release raised, drawer closed. Exact dimensions, materials and poses are in README.md and task.py.
metadata.scoring: 0.5 for guide seated and keeper closed with hands clear. 1.0 if locked before release, drawer travels at least 48 mm in 3 s, sleeve clears the guide, and both conditions hold for 2 s. Permanent 0 if a plug backs out more than 2 mm, a guide falls or comes loose during proof, or a gripper enters the protected area during proof. All other outcomes score 0.
metadata.reset_notes: Return both inserts and sleeve to their start marks. Open the keeper, close and latch the drawer, and fully seat both plugs. Clear trial history.
metadata.fidelity: Rigid split guides and sleeve, jointed slack loop, compliant mock plugs, and a spring force driving a constrained carriage. Contact determines whether the sleeve passes. Gripper proximity is used to detect assistance. Jacket wear, electrical behaviour and fracture are outside the model.
metadata.scores: Dream-1: 0.0 in 800 steps. Scripted demo: 1.0 in 463 steps.

metadata.title: Put the right plugs of two devices in their holders when the cables run hidden under a cover
metadata.instruction: Put the plug of the red box's cable in the red holder and the plug of the blue box's cable in the blue holder. Leave the other plugs where they are.
metadata.context: When cables run hidden under a cover, a desk tray or a floor duct, which loose plug belongs to which device cannot be seen. Here five identical cables cross out of sight and every plug lies away from its own device, so looking does not answer the question: the robot has to tug a cable where it leaves its device and see which plug moves. Taking the wrong plug is the failure that matters, because it disconnects or moves the wrong device.
metadata.setup: Station table, positions in cm from the midpoint between the two arm bases projected onto the table (x forward away from the robot, y to the robot's left). Devices: five 9 x 9 x 7 cm boxes (3D-printed PLA or painted wooden blocks) fixed to the table, robot-facing side at x 53, centred at y +24 (yellow), +12 (red), 0 (green), -12 (blue) and -24 (orange). Cover: a grey 15 x 86 x 1 cm plate (PLA or plywood) spanning x 25 to 40 and y -43 to +43, its underside 2.5 cm above the table, on two 1 cm thick end walls at y +42.5 and -42.5, fixed to the table. Under the cover, hidden: ten smooth grey guide posts (PTFE), 4 cm diameter and 8 mm tall, fixed to the table, five at x 37.5 (y +21.3, +9.3, +2.7, -9.3, -21.3) and five at x 27.5 (y +27.3, +13.3, +4.7, -14.7, -25.3). Cables: five identical black 8 mm round PVC cords, each fixed (glued, with strain relief) into the robot-facing side of its box 1.3 cm above the table, each ending in an identical black 3D-printed PLA plug, 35 x 16 x 12 mm (long side along the cable), 15 g. Lengths: yellow 49.3, red 67.0, green 43.6, blue 69.0, orange 40.0 cm. Each cable comes down to the table within 5 cm (the yellow, red and orange ones leave their box turned 17, 9 and 6 degrees to the robot's right and straighten within 2 cm) and runs straight towards the robot along its box's centre line to the far row of posts, bends round one of them, runs diagonally under the cover, bends round a post of the near row and comes out of the cover straight towards the robot, its plug lying flat with its centre at x 17. The routes, by box: yellow from y +24 round posts (37.5, +21.3) and (27.5, +4.7) to its plug at y +2; red from y +12 round (37.5, +9.3) and (27.5, -25.3) to y -28; green from y 0 round (37.5, +2.7) and (27.5, +13.3) to y +16; blue from y -12 round (37.5, -9.3) and (27.5, +27.3) to y +30; orange from y -24 round (37.5, -21.3) and (27.5, -14.7) to y -12. Every bend wraps its post at 2.7 cm from the post's centre. Where two diagonals cross, the later one in the laying order blue, red, yellow, green, orange lies on top (red over blue, yellow over blue, green over yellow, red and blue, orange over red). Plug holders: two U-channels (3D-printed PLA) fixed to the table on either side of the midline, each with two side walls 45 mm long (along x), 4 mm thick and 8 mm tall, 40 mm apart (inner slot 45 x 40 mm, the table is its floor), closed on the robot side by a white end stop 4 mm thick, 48 mm wide and 20 mm tall, open at the far end. The holder with blue side walls has its slot centre at x 11, y +18; the holder with red side walls at x 11, y -18.
metadata.scoring: Score 0 if at any moment the yellow, green or orange box's plug is more than 5 cm (3D) from where it lay at the start, whether picked up, pushed or slid by a tug on its cable (tape marks; judged from the top-camera video), or the red box's plug lies in the blue holder or the blue box's plug in the red holder; also 0 if a cable is pulled out of its box (its end at the box moves more than 1 cm). Boxes, cover, posts and holders are fixed to the table. A plug lies in a holder when it is between the holder's side walls, lying on the table, inside the slot or sticking out of its open far end by at most 1 cm. Otherwise, at the end: 1.0 if the red box's plug lies in the red holder and the blue box's plug in the blue holder, each released (no gripper within 3 cm of its centre); 0.5 if exactly one of the two lies released in its own holder; 0 otherwise, including doing nothing. Success (1.0) once the full condition has held for 1 s with both plugs at rest.
metadata.reset_notes: Lay the cables in the order blue, red, yellow, green, orange: each straight from its box along its box's centre line, round its far post, diagonally to its near post, round it and straight out to its plug mark at x 17, pulled snug against both posts. Plugs flat, long side along the cable. Remove anything from the holders.
metadata.fidelity: Each cable is a chain of 2 cm rigid segments with bending springs (no twist, no plasticity); plugs are rigid boxes; box ends are fixed. Boxes, cover, posts and holders are fixed rigid shapes; holders have no latch. Real cords kink less sharply at the posts and can twist. A real taut cable would stop the plug short of its holder; the simulated arm can pull harder, so each box fixing lets go above 300 N and a pulled-out cable scores 0 (same outcome).
